tagline: A Piedmont road in North Carolina’s state scenic byway program
intro: North Carolina’s scenic-byway program includes McAuley Road among its Piedmont routes.
Near Huntersville, Ramah Presbyterian Church’s present sanctuary dates to 1881, while the oldest burials in its cemetery date to about 1800.
Another Huntersville landmark, the John F. Ewart farmhouse, was built in 1898 and moved to Centennial Forest Drive in 2006.

moments.title: John F. Ewart Farm
moments.text: The John F. Ewart farmhouse was built in 1898, but its address changed in 2006 when the house moved to Centennial Forest Drive in Huntersville. Its design is a two-story I-house with a rear kitchen wing, two exterior brick chimneys and a gabled front porch. The farm district entered the National Register in 1991, before that relocation.

moments.title: Oehler Nature Preserve
moments.text: In August 2020, two teenagers found gasoline bubbling from the ground in Oehler Nature Preserve near Huntersville. The leak came from the buried Colonial Pipeline. Colonial later reported that its pipeline had failed on July 27, at least eighteen days before the discovery. In July 2022, the company estimated that at least two million gallons had escaped. That month, a court approved a consent decree requiring further testing, a cleanup plan and penalties.

moments.title: Ramah Presbyterian Church and Cemetery
moments.text: Ramah Presbyterian Church’s frame sanctuary dates to 1881. The rectangular building combines vernacular Greek Revival and Italianate design, with a front-facing gable and arched sash windows. A log fellowship building followed in 1935. The cemetery’s oldest burials date to about 1800, predating the current sanctuary. It contains approximately 500 burials.
